slides.title: Background : Contrastive Learning

blocks.text: Background : Contrastive Learning
· The model learns to make representations of images from the same source similar, and representations
of images from different sources as dissimilar as possible.
![image](/image/placeholder)

slides.raw_text: Background : Contrastive Learning · The model learns to make representations of images from the same source similar, and representations of images from different sources as dissimilar as possible. ![image](/image/placeholder)

slides.title: Background : CLIP

blocks.text: Background : CLIP
· CLIP(Contrastive Language-Image Pre-Training)
· This model uses contrastive learning, and applies it across different modalities-images and texts.
· By aligning image representations and text representations in a shared embedding space, it enables joint
learning between modalities.
![image](/image/placeholder)
Radford et al., "Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision," ICML 2021

slides.raw_text: Background : CLIP · CLIP(Contrastive Language-Image Pre-Training) · This model uses contrastive learning, and applies it across different modalities-images and texts. · By aligning image representations and text representations in a shared embedding space, it enables joint learning between modalities. ![image](/image/placeholder) Radford et al., "Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision," ICML 2021

slides.title: Motivation & Intro

blocks.text: Motivation & Intro
1. Opportunity:

The widespread adoption of wearable IMU sensors has dramatically increased the value and potential of
motion data.
2. Problem:

Manual annotation-driven IMU models suffer from high labeling costs and poor generalization to new
activities.
3. Inspiration:
Inspired by BERT/GPT and CLIP, multimodal contrastive pre-training.

"What if we could pre-train IMU exactly like CLIP does for images and text-
and get rich, semantic embeddings without any labels?"
IMU2CLIP
" Let's build an IMU-CLIP: multimodal IMU↔Video/Text contrastive pre-train! "

slides.title: Future Work

blocks.text: Future Work
Exploring Multimodal Reasoning with LLMs

· Leverage IMU2CLIP's sensor-to-text translation capability to enable complex multimodal reasoning
tasks.
· Integrate IMU-derived textual descriptions with Large Language Models (LLMs) to answer
summarization and memory recall queries about user activities.

· This approach offers a promising direction for developing low-power, video-free contextual AI in wearable
devices.

slides.title: Contribution

blocks.text: Contribution
Key Contributions of this paper
1. A novel large-scale pre-training approach for IMU sensors is proposed.
2. An in-depth empirical analysis evaluating the pre-trained models is provided for both upstream
and downstream fine-tuning tasks.

3. Lastly, novel applications are presented that show the feasibility of a wider usage for IMU sensor
signals.

slides.title: 1. Limitations

blocks.text: Limitation & Points to Consider
1. Limitations

· Frozen CLIP Encoders: The reliance on pre-trained and frozen CLIP encoders for video-text alignment might
limit the model's ability to fully adapt to or learn novel inter-modal relationships specific to IMU data. This could
potentially restrict the nuanced learning of video-text context from the perspective of motion.
![image](/image/placeholder)
2. Points to Consider

· Generalization to Third-Person Views: The current evaluation primarily uses egocentric (first-person)
datasets. Future work should investigate the model's performance and generalizability when applied to third-
person video data, which represents different visual perspectives and motion patterns.
